1.content:
CASE COVER AND PARTIES
Riverside Development LLC v. Harbor Construction Partners, Inc. Confidential case record prepared for counsel review. The dispute concerns a mixed-use redevelopment project at 114 Riverside Avenue, New York. Riverside is the owner and Harbor is the general contractor.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 1 OF 50

2.content:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Riverside alleges that Harbor missed contractual milestones, submitted unsupported payment applications, and failed to correct defective waterproofing. Harbor denies material breach and contends that owner-directed design changes, permit delays, and late site access excused the schedule impact.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 2 OF 50

3.content:
PARTIES AND REPRESENTATIVES
Plaintiff/Owner: Riverside Development LLC, represented by Northstar Legal Group. Defendant/Contractor: Harbor Construction Partners, Inc., represented by Vance & Cole LLP. Architect: Meridian Studio Architects. Lender: Hudson Commercial Bank.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 3 OF 50

4.content:
PROJECT DESCRIPTION
The project is a twelve-story mixed-use building with 184 residential units, ground-floor retail, two levels of below-grade parking, and a public riverwalk. The contract price is $48,600,000, subject to approved change orders.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 4 OF 50

5.content:
CONTRACT FORMATION
The parties executed the Master Construction Agreement on January 18, 2024. The agreement incorporates the plans, specifications, general conditions, schedule of values, and the dispute-resolution exhibit. The planned substantial-completion date was June 30, 2025.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 5 OF 50

6.content:
SCHEDULE BASELINE
The baseline schedule identifies excavation, foundation, structural frame, enclosure, mechanical rough-in, finishes, testing, and turnover as critical activities. Harbor was required to update the schedule monthly and identify activities that threatened substantial completion.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 6 OF 50

7.content:
ARTICLE 3 - NOTICE OF DELAY
A party discovering a material delay shall provide written notice within ten business days. The notice must identify the affected milestone, expected impact, and mitigation steps. Failure to provide timely notice may limit recovery for delay damages.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 7 OF 50

8.content:
SITE ACCESS AND CONDITIONS
Riverside delivered the initial site on February 1, 2024. Harbor reported undocumented utility lines on February 12. The parties agreed that investigation would proceed without stopping unaffected work, while responsibility for verified owner-caused conditions remained reserved.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 8 OF 50

9.content:
PERMIT HISTORY
The foundation permit issued February 26, 2024. The Department of Buildings issued comments on the facade package in May. Meridian submitted a revised package on June 4, and the facade permit was issued July 9, 2024.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 9 OF 50

10.content:
DESIGN DOCUMENTS
The issued-for-construction drawings dated January 10, 2024 govern unless modified by a signed change order or written architect instruction. Harbor was required to review dimensions and promptly report inconsistencies discovered during coordination.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 10 OF 50

11.content:
DEFAULT NOTICE
On November 14, 2024, Riverside issued a preliminary notice identifying schedule slippage, incomplete submittals, and deficient waterproofing. The notice requested a recovery schedule within seven days and reserved all contractual remedies.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 11 OF 50

12.content:
ARTICLE 5 - CURE PERIOD
The receiving party has thirty calendar days after valid notice to cure a material breach, unless an emergency threatens immediate and irreparable harm. A cure plan must state responsible personnel, corrective work, and the date by which compliance will be achieved.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 12 OF 50

13.content:
HARBOR RESPONSE
Harbor responded on November 21, 2024, disputing the characterization of delay and attributing six weeks to owner revisions. Harbor proposed extended shifts, additional waterproofing crews, and weekly executive meetings.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 13 OF 50

14.content:
RECOVERY SCHEDULE
The recovery schedule moved interior framing to parallel work fronts and added Saturday shifts. The schedule forecast substantial completion on August 15, 2025, subject to timely release of the elevator shop drawings and final facade approvals.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 14 OF 50

15.content:
MEETING MINUTES
The December 3 coordination meeting recorded open issues for facade anchors, elevator dimensions, fire-stopping details, and roof drains. Meridian directed Harbor to submit a consolidated request for information log within five business days.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 15 OF 50

16.content:
ARTICLE 16 - INSURANCE
Harbor shall maintain commercial general liability, workers compensation, automobile liability, and builder risk coverage. Certificates must name Riverside and the lender as additional insureds where required, and cancellation notices must be provided before coverage terminates.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 16 OF 50

17.content:
INSURANCE CERTIFICATES
The certificate dated January 30, 2024 listed $2,000,000 per occurrence general liability and $5,000,000 umbrella coverage. Riverside requested an endorsement showing completed-operations coverage; Harbor supplied the endorsement on March 6.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 17 OF 50

18.content:
ARTICLE 8 - PAYMENT OBLIGATIONS
Riverside must pay an approved payment application within twenty-five days after receipt of the architect certification. Harbor must support each application with conditional waivers, updated schedule information, stored-material evidence, and a current schedule of values.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 18 OF 50

19.content:
PAYMENT APPLICATION 09
Application 09 requested $3,240,000 gross, less retainage and prior payments. Meridian certified $2,610,000 after excluding unsupported stored materials and work not conforming to the inspection log. Riverside paid the certified amount.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 19 OF 50

20.content:
PAYMENT DISPUTE
Harbor claimed the withheld amount was an improper setoff. Riverside responded that the contract permits withholding for defective work and incomplete substantiation, provided the owner gives written reasons and releases undisputed amounts.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 20 OF 50

21.content:
WATERPROOFING OBSERVATIONS
Inspection reports dated October 8 and October 22 identified membrane holidays, inadequate laps, and unsealed penetrations at the parking garage north wall. Harbor was directed to expose representative areas and submit a repair method.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 21 OF 50

22.content:
REMEDIATION PLAN
Harbor proposed removing affected membrane, drying the substrate, applying primer, installing replacement membrane, and performing a flood test. Meridian approved the method subject to photographic records and a twenty-four-hour test period.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 22 OF 50

23.content:
QUALITY CONTROL
The quality-control log records remedial work at grid lines N-4 through N-9. A December 19 test passed at the north wall, but a January 7 retest failed at one penetration. Harbor reopened the area and completed a second repair.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 23 OF 50

24.content:
ARTICLE 10 - CHANGE ORDERS
No change in contract sum or time is enforceable as a change order unless documented in a written instrument signed by Riverside and Harbor. Emergency direction may proceed to protect life or property, but pricing and time must be submitted promptly.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 24 OF 50

25.content:
CHANGE ORDER 04
Change Order 04 adds $186,400 for revised retail storefront mullions and grants fourteen calendar days. It was signed by both parties on August 16, 2024, and incorporated into the next schedule update.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 25 OF 50

26.content:
CHANGE DIRECTIVES
Three architect directives addressed fire-rated shaft walls and corridor ceiling access panels. Harbor priced the work but proceeded before signatures. Riverside maintains that only the signed directive for shaft walls qualifies for additional compensation.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 26 OF 50

27.content:
OWNER-CAUSED DELAYS
The record supports a nine-day delay associated with late selection of lobby stone. Harbor did not segregate that delay from concurrent facade and procurement delays, making the claimed forty-two-day extension difficult to verify.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 27 OF 50

28.content:
CONTRACTOR-CAUSED DELAYS
The critical-path report identifies late elevator submittals, insufficient framing labor, and repeated waterproofing repairs as contractor-responsible impacts. Harbor disputes causation and points to late design clarifications.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 28 OF 50

29.content:
CONCURRENT DELAY ANALYSIS
The schedule expert concludes that owner and contractor delays overlapped from October 2 through October 11, 2024. The report recommends no compensable delay damages for that period but allows evaluation of non-overlapping impacts.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 29 OF 50

30.content:
DAMAGES OVERVIEW
Riverside claims liquidated damages, consultant fees, temporary security, and carrying costs. Harbor claims unpaid change work, extended general conditions, and acceleration costs. Both parties reserve rights concerning consequential damages under the contract limitation.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 30 OF 50

31.content:
ARTICLE 13 - INDEMNIFICATION
Harbor shall defend and indemnify Riverside from claims arising out of Harbor operations to the extent caused by Harbor or its subcontractors. The obligation does not require indemnity for Riverside's sole negligence or intentional misconduct.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 31 OF 50

32.content:
THIRD-PARTY CLAIM
A neighboring owner alleged vibration damage during excavation. Harbor notified its carrier and retained a geotechnical consultant. The claim was resolved without admission for $92,000, with the parties disputing allocation of the settlement and defense costs.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 32 OF 50

33.content:
SUBCONTRACTOR ISSUES
Metro Waterproofing submitted a notice of nonpayment and threatened demobilization. Harbor provided a payment ledger showing disputed backcharges. Riverside requested proof of payment and conditional lien waivers before releasing the next progress payment.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 33 OF 50

34.content:
LIENS AND WAIVERS
A preliminary lien notice was received from Metro Waterproofing on February 2, 2025. Harbor obtained a release through January 31 but had not secured a final release for February work when Application 12 was submitted.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 34 OF 50

35.content:
SAFETY RECORD
The project recorded two OSHA-reportable incidents involving subcontractor employees. The safety consultant found no willful violation but required a revised fall-protection plan, daily toolbox talks, and documented corrective-action reviews.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 35 OF 50

36.content:
ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS
Testing identified petroleum-impacted soil near the former loading area. The environmental consultant recommended segregated excavation and disposal at a licensed facility. The parties treated the work as a potential allowance item pending laboratory confirmation.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 36 OF 50

37.content:
ARTICLE 16 - INSURANCE CLAIM
The builder-risk policy covers direct physical loss caused by a covered peril, subject to exclusions and deductible. Riverside notified the carrier after a storm damaged temporary roof protection. The carrier accepted coverage for emergency drying but reserved rights on consequential delay.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 37 OF 50

38.content:
STORM EVENT
A severe storm on March 18, 2025 caused water intrusion at the east stair core. Harbor installed temporary protection within twenty-four hours. Meridian's inspection found damage to gypsum board and insulation, with no structural damage.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 38 OF 50

39.content:
TESTING AND COMMISSIONING
The commissioning plan requires functional testing for HVAC, life safety, elevators, domestic water, and emergency power. Each system must have a signed test report, deficiency list, and closeout date before substantial completion.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 39 OF 50

40.content:
SUBSTANTIAL COMPLETION
Riverside may issue a certificate of substantial completion when the work is sufficiently complete for its intended use, subject to a punch list. The certificate does not waive latent defects, unresolved payment claims, or warranty rights.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 40 OF 50

41.content:
PUNCH LIST
The April 2025 punch list contains 214 items, including door hardware, paint touch-up, life-safety labels, facade sealant, and apartment finish corrections. Harbor closed 163 items by May 12 and disputed 18 as owner changes.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 41 OF 50

42.content:
WARRANTY OBLIGATIONS
Harbor warrants construction in accordance with the contract and must correct covered defects reported during the warranty period. Manufacturer warranties for equipment must be assigned to Riverside at closeout.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 42 OF 50

43.content:
ARTICLE 19 - GOVERNING LAW
The agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. The parties consent to courts located in New York County for permitted judicial proceedings.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 43 OF 50

44.content:
DISPUTE RESOLUTION
The parties must first meet through executive representatives, then participate in mediation before filing a covered claim in court. Emergency injunctive relief and lien remedies are preserved where the agreement permits.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 44 OF 50

45.content:
MEDIATION POSITION
Riverside seeks a completion plan, credit for defective work, and allocation of delay costs. Harbor seeks payment of certified change work, recognition of owner-caused delay, and release of withheld retainage subject to agreed security.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 45 OF 50

46.content:
EXPERT REPORT SUMMARY
The scheduling expert finds that Harbor failed to maintain a reliable contemporaneous schedule after September 2024. The cost expert can verify direct costs but cannot substantiate the full acceleration claim because daily labor records are incomplete.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 46 OF 50

47.content:
EVIDENCE INDEX
Key evidence includes the Master Construction Agreement, baseline schedule, meeting minutes, inspection reports, payment applications 09 through 12, Change Order 04, insurance certificates, photographs, expert reports, and correspondence exchanged between November 2024 and May 2025.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 47 OF 50

48.content:
ARTICLE 22 - TERMINATION
Riverside may terminate for uncured material breach after written notice and expiration of the applicable cure period. Immediate termination is permitted for insolvency, abandonment, repeated safety violations, or failure to maintain required insurance, subject to the agreement.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 48 OF 50

49.content:
REMEDIES AND RESERVATIONS
The parties reserve all claims, defenses, offsets, lien rights, warranty rights, and remedies available under the agreement and applicable law. No summary in this record constitutes a final legal conclusion or admission by either party.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 49 OF 50

50.content:
COUNSEL REVIEW CHECKLIST
Confirm notice dates and contractual deadlines. Reconcile the critical-path analysis with daily reports. Obtain executed change-order signatures. Verify insurance endorsements and lien waivers. Evaluate cure compliance, termination prerequisites, and New York governing-law implications before advising on next steps.
RIVERSIDE DEVELOPMENT DISPUTE | CONFIDENTIAL LEGAL WORK PRODUCT | PAGE 50 OF 50

chunks.content: A party must provide written notice of a material delay and allow the contractual cure period before pursuing remedies.
Notice must identify the affected milestone, the anticipated impact, and the action requested from the receiving party.
The delayed party shall provide written notice within ten (10) business days after discovering the delay. The notice must describe the cause, expected duration, and mitigation steps.
Failure to provide timely notice may limit recovery to losses that could not reasonably have been avoided.
Either party may terminate for material breach after written notice and an opportunity to cure.
A termination notice must be delivered in writing and specify the material breach relied upon by the terminating party.
Accrued payment obligations and confidentiality duties survive termination of this agreement.
